## The pattern

- Batch processing in motiongrammar means running the same pipeline over a folder of session files and stacking the results
- The template system is what makes this safe: one `csv_template` or `api_stream_template` object is defined once and reused for every file — column mappings, coordinate system, and skip rows are identical across sessions
- Each session returns its own `motion_trace`; summaries are extracted with `quantitate()` and bound together with `dplyr::bind_rows()`

---

## Minimal example — GPS CSV folder

```r
library(motiongrammar)
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# 1. Load the template once — defined from a representative file
template <- load_csv_template("catapult_template.xml")

# 2. Find all session files
session_files <- list.files("data/sessions/", pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)

# 3. Define the pipeline as a function
process_session <- function(path) {
  player_id  <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(path))
  desig_file <- file.path("data/labels", paste0(player_id, "_labels.csv"))

  initiate(session = path, template = template) |>
    coordinate(norm = TRUE) |>
    interpolate(hz = 10, max_gap_frames = 20) |>
    filtrate(method = "butterworth", target = "coordinates", cutoff = 1.5) |>
    derivate(derivatives = c("velocity", "acceleration", "angular_velocity")) |>
    designate(method = "manual", file = desig_file) |>
    elaborate(curved_load = velocity * angular_velocity) |>
    allocate_csv(file = "data/bands/gps_standard.csv")
}

# 4. Run across all files — purrr::map returns a named list of motion_trace objects
traces <- set_names(session_files, basename(session_files)) |>
  map(safely(process_session))

# 5. Separate successes from failures
ok     <- keep(traces, ~ is.null(.$error))
failed <- keep(traces, ~ !is.null(.$error))

if (length(failed) > 0) {
  message(length(failed), " session(s) failed:")
  walk(failed, ~ message("  ", .$error$message))
}

processed <- map(ok, "result")
```

---

## Extracting summaries

```r
# Run quantitate on each processed trace, tag with session name
summaries <- imap(processed, function(trace, session_name) {
  quantitate(
    trace,
    allocation  = "gps_standard",
    derivative  = "velocity",
    scope       = "designation",
    active_only = TRUE,
    time_s      = n() / 10,
    peak_vel    = max(velocity, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_hr     = mean(HeartRate, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
    mutate(session = session_name, .before = 1)
})

# Stack into one table
all_sessions <- bind_rows(summaries)
```

---

## Adding player metadata

```r
# If player metadata lives in the file path or a lookup table
player_meta <- readr::read_csv("data/player_roster.csv")
# columns: session_file, player_id, position, age

all_sessions <- all_sessions |>
  left_join(player_meta, by = c("session" = "session_file"))
```

---

## Collecting quality logs

```r
# Pull quality logs from every trace into one list — keyed by session name
quality_logs <- map(processed, ~ attr(.x, 'quality'))

# Check for issues across all sessions
issues_by_session <- imap(quality_logs, function(qual, session) {
  interp_issues <- qual$interpolate[[length(qual$interpolate)]]$issues
  if (!is.null(interp_issues)) {
    tibble(session = session, step = "interpolate", issue = interp_issues)
  }
}) |>
  bind_rows()

issues_by_session
```

---

## Parallelisation

- The pipeline is stateless per session — there are no shared objects
- Use `furrr::future_map()` as a drop-in replacement for `purrr::map()` to parallelise across CPU cores

```r
library(furrr)
plan(multisession, workers = 4)

processed <- set_names(session_files, basename(session_files)) |>
  future_map(safely(process_session), .progress = TRUE)

plan(sequential)  # reset
```

---

## Saving batch output

```r
# Save each processed trace as RDS — preserves full quality log
walk2(processed, names(processed), function(trace, name) {
  saveRDS(trace, file.path("output/traces", paste0(name, ".rds")))
})

# Save the stacked summary table
readr::write_csv(all_sessions, "output/session_summaries.csv")

# Save all quality logs as a single RDS
saveRDS(quality_logs, "output/quality_logs_batch.rds")
```

---

## Common failure modes in batch runs

- **Missing label file** — `designate(method = 'manual')` will error if the designation CSV doesn't exist; wrap in `safely()` and log failures
- **Different device firmware across sessions** — column names may drift between firmware versions; use `guess_csv_template()` on a suspicious file to check, then update the template
- **Variable Hz across sessions** — if `hz` varies by device or firmware, read `meta$native_hz` from metadata after `initiate()` and pass it explicitly to `interpolate()`
- **Timezone issues** — `initiate()` normalises all timestamps to Unix time (UTC); verify `native_hz` and `start_time` in `metadata_report()` for each session if results look temporally misaligned

```r
# Defensive hz resolution
process_session_safe <- function(path) {
  trace <- initiate(session = path, template = template)
  hz    <- attr(trace, 'metadata')$native_hz %||% 10L

  trace |>
    coordinate(norm = TRUE) |>
    interpolate(hz = hz, max_gap_frames = as.integer(hz * 2))
    # ... rest of pipeline
}
```
